fatal_errors: The proposed FeCrCoNiMo0.2 alloy is not the studied AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA.
SS316 is incorrectly substituted for the DS2205 comparator.
The proposed 250 °C, 3.5% NaCl, 50 N conditions conflict with the tested 25–100 °C deionized-water, 5–15 N regime; liquid-water testing at 250 °C would also require a specified pressurized apparatus.
The claimed 30% reduction and 0.5 mg/h threshold are unsupported by evidence.
The hypothesis omits the retained L12/B2 lamellar microstructure, thermal-shock phase stability, and nonmonotonic minimum degradation near 50 °C.
explanation: The response aligns only with the broad premise that an HEA may outperform conventional stainless steel in elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion. It reconstructs neither the material nor the comparator, intervention, environmental conditions, or measured outcomes. Its dense-oxide-barrier mechanism has limited generic overlap with passive-film and tribo-layer protection, but it misses the central role of the stable L12/B2 lamellar structure, temperature-dependent depassivation/repassivation balance, and film disruption at 100 °C. The proposed head-to-head experiment and falsification threshold are testable, but the setup is underspecified and potentially infeasible at 250 °C without pressure control. With no cited evidence, its composition-specific and quantitative claims are unsupported.
